notes:
Sources: blumob.com.br (schedule landing page links out to bus2.info + BluMob app; no inline tables), onibus.online/empresas/blumob (full route list: 96 lines by class + trunk line names/vias), Blumenau SETERB official page (6 named terminals with street addresses, service structure: 12 trunk / 64 feeder / 4 health lines + Madrugueira midnight-04:00 night service, fares R$5.50 pre-paid / R$6.80 on-board). bus2.info report and per-line pages are JS-rendered and were NOT machine-fetchable, so exact per-stop street sequences and published clock times per line could not be extracted.

What IS well-evidenced and modeled faithfully: the 6 official urban terminals (names + addresses), the full trunk-line list with real names/vias (10 via Rua São Paulo, 11 via 2 de Setembro, 12 via Escola Agrícola, 15 via Ponte Tamarindo, 30 via Gov. Jorge Lacerda, 31 via Rua dos Caçadores, 32 via Água Verde, 70 Proeb/Aterro, 80 via Pedro Zimmermann, 81 via Gustavo Zimmermann, 82 via Jacob Ineichen), and the Interbairros/Alimentador integration structure.

What is APPROXIMATE / synthesized (hence confidence 0.42): stop coordinates — only Terminal Aterro is precisely anchored (-26.8709,-49.0954, taxi stand at the terminal); the other 5 terminals are geocoded from their documented street addresses/neighborhoods (WGS-84, correct ~±300m). Trips are anchored ONLY at terminals (no intermediate street stops, since per-line stop sequences were not extractable) and use even headways across the documented service span (day service ~05:00–24:00, Madrugueira 24:00–04:00) rather than the real published timetable. No stops were invented — every stop is a documented SETERB terminal.

This is a terminal-level trunk-network skeleton, not a full stop-level feed. A faithful full feed needs the bus2.info per-line tables or the BluMob app GTFS.
